mutations.because: Removing the opening-vs-matched check restores the old behaviour: an unclosed or malformed fence simply never matches FENCE, the lane disappears from the check, and parsePremises returns quietly.
The check must fire only on a genuine loss; a >= throws on every well-formed document, so the parse tests pin the boundary.

Dropping the range filter re-introduces the false positive this fix closes: an opener-shaped line inside a closed premise body (a heredoc quoting ```premise B) is counted as an opening again, so a valid plan throws UNCLOSED and aborts the whole verification run.
